s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Gaya session of the Indian National Congress in December 1922:
1. C.R. Das presided over the session.
2. The resolution advocating council entry was rejected.
3. The rejection led C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru to resign from their Congress positions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. At Gaya, C.R. Das’s council-entry resolution was rejected, after which Das and Motilal Nehru resigned and announced the new party on 31 December 1922.
tq: Check the connected sequence of session, resolution and resignations.

s: Which statement best expresses the broad significance of the Swarajist and No-Changer activities during the 1922–28 lull?
o: Constructive work was abandoned after the formation of the Swaraj Party.
Council work completely replaced mass mobilisation and constructive work.
The national movement became inactive until the 1930s.
Council work and constructive work were ultimately complementary to the national movement.
x: The Swarajists kept the national movement active through council work, while the No-Changers sustained constructive work. These approaches were regarded as complementary and were reconciled at Belgaum in 1924.
tq: Compare the two approaches by their functions and identify their combined significance.

s: Which of the following correctly represents the principal difference between the Swarajists and the No-Changers?
o: Swarajists favoured council entry, whereas No-Changers emphasised constructive work.
Swarajists supported constructive work, whereas No-Changers supported council entry.
Both groups rejected council entry and constructive work alike.
Both groups favoured cooperation with the colonial government.
x: The Swarajists favoured entry into the councils, while the No-Changers concentrated on constructive work and continued the boycott. Both groups were reunited at Belgaum in 1924.
tq: Use the central contrast in policy rather than confusing the groups’ common nationalist objective.
